transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I'm sorry to take up your time, but my daughter really persuaded me to come in today. I just can't shake this feeling that I'm a burden to everyone around me and that I've let my whole community down.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people do not, or have you had any strong beliefs that others say are not true?

It's really hard to admit, but I keep hearing a man's voice behind my left ear telling me I'm useless and that the kids would be safer if I wasn't there. I also can't shake the feeling that parents and city officials are secretly watching me at my crosswalk and keeping tabs to prove I'm unfit for my job.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression with hallucinations or strong false beliefs like this before, or is this the first time it has happened?

No, this is the very first time I've ever experienced anything like this. It all started about a year and a half ago when my marriage began to fall apart, but before that, I never heard those voices, felt watched, or felt this deeply depressed.
Have you had any thoughts of wanting to die or of hurting yourself, or made any plans to do so?

Yes... for months now, I've caught myself thinking it would just be easier for everyone if I didn't wake up. On my worst days at the crosswalk, I picture stepping off the curb in front of a truck, and I actually have to grip the stop sign pole to keep myself from getting too close to the street.
Have there been any periods of at least 2 months in the past year when you felt completely back to your usual self, with the depression, voices, and suspicious beliefs gone?

No, I haven't had any periods where I felt completely back to normal. Ever since things started falling apart with my marriage about a year and a half ago, this heavy cloud and the strange experiences have been pretty much constant. Even if the sadness or the voices eased up slightly for a brief moment, I never had a stretch of two months where everything was gone and I felt like myself.
Have you ever had any other episodes in the past where you were depressed, with or without hearing voices or having unusual beliefs, even if they improved for a while?
No, I've never had any episodes like this in the past. These awful feelings and the voices only started after my marriage began to fall apart about a year and a half ago.
Have these symptoms—your depression, hearing the voice, and feeling watched—been present continuously for at least 2 weeks at a time without fully going away?

Yes, it has been much longer than two weeks—both the heavy, depressed feelings and the experiences of hearing the voice and feeling watched have been going on continuously for over a year now. It has been a constant struggle that hasn't really let up at all in all that time.
Have you ever had any earlier episodes of depression, with or without hearing voices or feeling watched, before this current one?

No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. These heavy feelings and the other things I've been going through only started after my marriage began to fall apart over the last couple of years.
Have you ever had any earlier episodes of depression, even without hallucinations or suspicious beliefs, before this current one?

No, I've never had any issues with depression or my mental health before this. I was always a very active, busy person in the community until my marriage fell apart. This is really the first time I've ever felt this kind of darkness or low mood.
Have you ever had any previous episodes of depression before this one, even if they did not include hearing voices or feeling watched?
I don't recall ever having any previous episodes of depression before this. These feelings only really started about a year and a half ago when my marriage began to fall apart.
Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or felt overly confident or reckless?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. If anything, I've felt completely the opposite—just incredibly heavy, slow, and deeply depressed.
Has this current period of depression lasted for at least 2 weeks continuously, with most of the day feeling depressed or losing interest in things?

Yes, it has been much longer than two weeks—it has actually been going on for over a year now. Almost every single day, I wake up with this heavy, hopeless feeling in my chest and just can't bring myself to care about my church or community events anymore.
Do the voice and the feeling that people are watching you only happen when your depression is at its worst, or do they ever continue even when your mood feels a bit better?

They actually do continue even when my mood is a bit better. Last fall, there was a spell where my sadness had eased up enough that I could get through my shifts without crying, but I still heard that man's voice criticizing me and was sure the school district was secretly collecting evidence against me.
Do the voices or suspicious beliefs ever continue for at least 2 weeks when you are not feeling depressed at all, or do they only happen during times when your depression is present?

Yes, that spell last fall actually lasted for a few weeks where the depression and sadness were gone. Even though I wasn't feeling down during those weeks, I still heard the man's voice criticizing me and felt convinced the school district was secretly collecting evidence on me.
Have you ever had at least 2 weeks when you were not depressed at all, but you still heard the voice or felt that people were watching or following you?

Yes, that's exactly what happened last fall. For a few weeks, my sadness eased up and I could get through my shifts without crying, but I still heard that man's voice criticizing me. I also remained convinced that the school district was secretly collecting evidence on me, even though I didn't feel down during those weeks.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had hallucinations or suspicious beliefs but no depression or low mood at all?

Yes, that is exactly what happened during that spell last fall. My sadness had lifted enough that I wasn't feeling down or crying during my shifts, but I still heard that man's voice criticizing me and remained convinced the school district was secretly gathering evidence against me.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had hallucinations or suspicious beliefs but no depression or low mood at all?

Yes, as I mentioned, during that spell last fall my sadness had eased up and I wasn't crying during my shifts. But even though my mood was okay for those few weeks, I still heard that man's voice criticizing me and believed the school district was secretly gathering evidence against me.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had hallucinations or suspicious beliefs but no depression or low mood at all?

Yes, that's right. During that spell last fall, my sadness lifted for a few weeks and I wasn't crying at work, but I still heard that man's voice criticizing me. I also remained completely convinced that the school district was secretly collecting evidence to prove I was unfit.
Have you noticed a clear decline in your work, self-care, or ability to think and function over this time, such as becoming much more disorganized, withdrawn, or unable to keep up with daily tasks?

Yes, there has been a huge decline. I've cut way back on church, missed my crossing guard shifts, and let my apartment and bills slide so much that my daughter has to constantly check on me to make sure I'm keeping up. My mind just feels too foggy all the time to think straight or make even the simplest decisions.

Have you ever had a clear episode of mania or hypomania, such as several days of feeling unusually energized, needing much less sleep, talking more than usual, or becoming unusually confident or reckless?

No, I have never had any episodes like that. It has been the exact opposite for me, where I just feel constantly heavy, slow, and deeply depressed. I've never had times where I felt high energy, needed less sleep, or felt unusually confident.

Have you noticed any symptoms like speaking very little, having trouble starting or finishing tasks, seeming emotionally flat, or becoming confused or disorganized even when your mood is not depressed?

Yes, I feel completely emotionally flat, like the light inside me has gone out, and my mind is so foggy that even picking a shirt is hard and it takes me a few seconds just to get my words out. These struggles are definitely worst when I'm feeling really low, but the mental fog and lack of motivation still linger even when the heavy sadness lifts a bit.
Have you ever had hallucinations, delusions, or a clear decline in functioning for at least 2 weeks when you were not depressed at all and not having any mood symptoms?

Yes, that's exactly what happened last fall. My sadness lifted for a few weeks and I wasn't crying at my shifts, but I still heard that man's voice criticizing me. I also remained completely convinced that the school district was secretly collecting evidence to prove I was unfit.
Have you ever had at least 2 weeks when you had no depression or other mood symptoms at all, but you still heard voices or believed people were watching or plotting against you?

Yes, that definitely happened during a period last fall. My sadness eased up a bit and I wasn't crying during my shifts, but I still heard that man's voice criticizing me. I also remained convinced that the school district was secretly collecting evidence on me to prove I was unfit.

During that time last fall when you were not feeling depressed, did you also have any problems with your thinking or speech, such as becoming very disorganized, hard to follow, or having trouble telling a clear story?
I don't recall having those kinds of speech or thinking problems during that time last fall. It was really just the voice and that feeling of being watched that were going on then.
During the times when you were not feeling depressed, did anyone notice that your speech became hard to follow, your thoughts felt very jumbled, or your behavior seemed disorganized?
No, I don't recall anyone ever mentioning that my speech or behavior seemed strange during those weeks. I certainly didn't feel like my thoughts were jumbled or disorganized at that time.
During the times when you were not feeling depressed, did you also have any periods of unusually high energy, decreased need for sleep, or feeling overly confident or irritable?

No, I've never had any periods of high energy, needing less sleep, or feeling overly confident like that. Even when my sadness wasn't at its absolute worst, I've only ever experienced the low mood and the other struggles I've already mentioned.

When your mood was not depressed last fall, did you still have any symptoms like hearing voices or feeling watched for at least 2 weeks, and did those symptoms happen without any mood symptoms at all?

Yes, that's correct. Last fall, there was a period of a few weeks where the heavy sadness lifted slightly and I wasn't crying through my shifts, but I still heard that man's voice criticizing me. I also still felt sure the school district was secretly collecting evidence on me, even though I didn't feel particularly depressed during those weeks.

During the times when you were hearing the voice or feeling watched, did you ever have at least 2 weeks when those psychotic symptoms were completely gone, even though your depression was still present?

I'm not entirely sure, but I don't recall the voice or the feeling of being watched ever completely disappearing for a full two weeks while I was feeling depressed. They might have quieted down a bit at times, but they never truly went away during those low periods.
When you were feeling depressed, did the voice or the feeling that people were watching you ever completely go away for at least 2 weeks while your depression was still present?

No, they didn't completely disappear. There were some weeks where the voice and the feeling of being watched let up a bit and weren't as intense, but they never fully went away. The heavy sadness and feeling like a burden have just been constant almost this entire time.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a prolonged mood episode with prominent depressive symptoms plus persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions). Importantly, psychotic symptoms clearly persisted for at least several weeks in the absence of any mood symptoms, and there is no history of mania/hypomania. This pattern is most consistent with schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.
